risks.title: Dependence on UniCredit and governance risk
risks.summary: FinecoBank must comply with directives issued by UniCredit as the parent holding company, under legal and regulatory coordination obligations. The Board of Directors must ensure the recepimento of group provisions, creating strategic and operational dependency on the parent company.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk located at the beginning of Item 1A. Intensive language regarding the recepimento of parent company directives and disposal powers. FinecoBank is controlled by UniCredit with compliance obligations to group directives. Stable trend but structural. High weight for a listed subsidiary.

risks.title: Risk of conflicts of interest with parent company UniCredit
risks.summary: Buy-sell transactions and obligations between FinecoBank and its executives or parent company UniCredit are subject to strict legal restrictions (art. 136 TUB). The risk of conflicts of interest is particularly high in intra-group transactions, especially involving Marina Natale, designated as Consigliere Esecutivo due to her role at UniCredit.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned under art. 136 TUB concerning transactions with executives and the parent company. Precise legal language indicating a major regulatory concern. Stable trend but inherent structural risk in intra-group relationships. Critical litigation/compliance category.

risks.title: Management of inside information and market abuse risk
risks.summary: FinecoBank maintains two inside information registers (Registro Fineco and Registro UCI), with risks of leaks or inadequate handling. The procedure requires complex coordination between the CFO of FinecoBank and the CFO of UniCredit to assess price sensitivity. Risk of market abuse and regulatory sanctions in case of failure.
risks.score_rationale: Section 5 entirely dedicated to inside information management procedures. Detailed and normative language indicating a major regulatory concern. Stable trend but increasing complexity due to dual status (listed subsidiary + controlled entity). High weight for CONSOB/Borsa Italiana compliance.

risks.title: Concentration of executive power in the Amministratore Delegato
risks.summary: The concentration of executive powers in a single individual (Alessandro Foti) creates a key person dependency risk. Although the Chairman (Enrico Cotta Ramusino) is independent, the lack of separation between CEO and COO roles reduces internal checks and increases succession risk.
risks.score_rationale: Alessandro Foti has held both Amministratore Delegato and Direttore Generale roles since July 2014. Neutral language but concentrated governance structure. Stable trend. Moderate weight but succession and personal dependency risks.

risks.title: Complex banking regulatory compliance risk
risks.summary: FinecoBank operates under a complex, multi-level banking regulatory framework (Banca d'Italia, CONSOB, Borsa Italiana, EU). Compliance obligations include risk management, capital adequacy, internal dealing procedures, and governance. Risk of non-compliance leading to regulatory sanctions.
risks.score_rationale: Multiple references to TUB, TUF, Banca d'Italia Circular No. 285, Code of Self-Regulation, Issuers' Regulation. Intensive technical and normative language. Stable trend but evolving regulatory environment. Very high weight for a bank.

risks.title: Risk of IT system failure and cybersecurity
risks.summary: FinecoBank manages sensitive registers (Registro Fineco, Registro UCI) and complex data flows via IT systems. Risk of cyberattacks, data loss, or communication system failures (e.g., Board videoconferences) that could compromise the confidentiality of inside information.
risks.score_rationale: Implied in the management of inside information registers and data flows. Moderate language but critical infrastructure for a digital bank. Trend up (increasing risk). Moderate weight but potentially high impact.

risks.title: Intense competition risk in the digital banking sector
risks.summary: FinecoBank operates in the digital banking/fintech segment where competition is intensifying (neobanks, fintechs, large digital banks). Risk of market share loss, margin compression, and need for continuous technology investments to remain competitive.
risks.score_rationale: Not explicitly detailed in the extract but implied in the fintech banking model. No language but highly competitive market context. Trend up (growing pressure). Moderate weight for a specialized subsidiary.

risks.title: Technology dependence and obsolescence risk
risks.summary: As a digital bank, FinecoBank heavily relies on technological infrastructure, digital platforms, and cybersecurity. Risk of technological obsolescence, system failures, high IT investment costs, and dependence on technology vendors.
risks.score_rationale: Implied in the digital banking model. No language but critical to the business model. Trend up (rapid technological evolution). Moderate weight but strategic risk.
